# Watch-Type Mobile Terminal for Payment Card Management

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a watch-type mobile terminal designed to conveniently search and manage payment cards, coupons, and membership cards used during payment transactions. As mobile payment technologies continue to advance, the ability to efficiently access and organize various payment-related items on a compact wearable device has become increasingly important. This invention addresses the need for an intuitive and user-friendly interface that allows users to quickly locate and select the appropriate payment method or associated benefit at the point of sale.

## System Architecture

The watch-type mobile terminal comprises several key components that work together to manage payment information effectively. These components include a display unit, a sensing unit, and a control unit. The display unit is responsible for presenting payment information to the user in a clear and accessible manner. The sensing unit detects user interactions with the device, while the control unit coordinates the overall operation of the terminal, processing input signals and determining how payment information is displayed and manipulated.

## Operational Method

### First Input Signal Detection

During operation, the control unit senses a first input signal directed at payment information displayed on the screen. This first input signal is characterized as a touch input in which the sensed area or applied pressure exceeds a predetermined threshold value. By distinguishing this type of input from ordinary touch interactions, the terminal can recognize the user's intent to engage more deeply with the displayed payment information.

### Displaying Indicators and Predetermined Items

In response to the first input signal, the control unit displays an indicator or a predetermined item that is included within the payment information. This functionality provides the user with immediate visual feedback and highlights relevant details, such as a specific payment card, coupon, or membership card associated with the transaction. The indicator serves to guide the user's attention and facilitate efficient navigation through available payment options.

### Enlarging Predetermined Items

Furthermore, the control unit is configured to enlarge and output the predetermined item in response to a second input signal. This enlargement feature enhances the visibility and readability of the selected item, which is particularly beneficial given the limited screen size of a watch-type device. By allowing users to expand specific payment items, the terminal ensures that critical information can be reviewed and confirmed with ease before completing a payment.

## Summary

Through the coordinated operation of the display unit, sensing unit, and control unit, the watch-type mobile terminal offers an efficient and intuitive solution for managing payment cards, coupons, and membership cards. The use of pressure- and area-sensitive touch inputs, combined with dynamic display and enlargement capabilities, enables users to conveniently search and select the appropriate payment information during transactions, thereby improving the overall user experience on wearable devices.

# Convenient Search of Payment Information on a Watch-Type Mobile Terminal

## Technical Field

The present invention relates to a watch-type mobile terminal and, more particularly, to a method and apparatus for conveniently searching and navigating payment-related information—such as payment cards, coupons, and membership cards—on a watch-type mobile terminal having a limited display area.

## Background of the Invention

With the growing popularity of mobile payment technologies, users increasingly rely on their mobile terminals to store and manage a wide variety of payment-related items. These items commonly include credit and debit cards, prepaid payment cards, discount coupons, and store membership cards. As the number of registered items grows, the ability to quickly locate and select a specific item becomes an important factor in the overall user experience.

Watch-type mobile terminals, however, present a unique challenge. Owing to their compact form factor, the display units of such devices are considerably smaller than those of conventional smartphones or tablets. Consequently, presenting numerous payment cards, coupons, and membership cards on a single screen—and allowing the user to browse among them efficiently—remains difficult. Conventional scrolling and selection methods, which are well suited to larger displays, often prove cumbersome and imprecise when applied to the limited display of a watch-type device.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention addresses the foregoing challenge by providing a watch-type mobile terminal that enables convenient searching of payment cards, coupons, and membership cards. To this end, the terminal includes a display unit configured to output payment information and a control unit configured to sense touch inputs applied to the display unit.

Rather than relying solely on the location of a touch, the control unit senses touch inputs on the basis of both the area of contact and the pressure applied to the display unit. Specifically, the control unit evaluates each touch input against one or more predetermined threshold values relating to touch area and touch pressure. This approach allows the terminal to distinguish between different types of user interactions even within a small display region.

Upon detecting a first input signal that exceeds the predetermined area and/or pressure values, the control unit displays an indicator or a predetermined item within the payment information. The indicator may, for example, identify a particular payment card, coupon, or membership card, or otherwise assist the user in navigating among the available items.

Subsequently, in response to a second input signal, the control unit enlarges the indicator or the predetermined item. By enlarging the relevant item, the terminal enables the user to view and select payment-related information more easily, notwithstanding the limited size of the display.

## Advantageous Effects

By sensing touch inputs based on area and pressure thresholds, and by progressively displaying and enlarging payment-related items in response to successive input signals, the present invention enables more efficient and user-friendly navigation of payment cards, coupons, and membership cards. As a result, a user of a watch-type mobile terminal can conveniently search for and select a desired payment item, even on a display of limited size, thereby improving the overall usability of mobile payment functions on such devices.

# The: The Most Common Word in English

The word "the" holds a remarkable place in the English language. Though small and often overlooked, it is the most frequently used word in English, appearing in nearly every sentence we speak or write. As the language's only definite article, "the" performs quiet but essential work in helping us communicate clearly.

## What "The" Does

"The" is a **definite article**, which means it points to a specific, known thing rather than something general. Consider the difference between these two sentences:

- "Please hand me *a* book." (any book)
- "Please hand me *the* book." (a particular book we both know about)

That single word transforms a vague request into a precise one. It signals that both speaker and listener share knowledge about which item is meant.

## A Brief History

"The" descends from Old English, where it evolved from a set of demonstrative words that also gave us "that" and "this." Originally, English had multiple forms that changed depending on gender, number, and grammatical role. Over centuries, these forms simplified into the single, unchanging "the" we use today—a rare example of a word that works the same way in every context.

## Why It Matters

Despite having no meaning of its own, "the" shapes how we understand the world around us. It helps distinguish the general from the specific, the familiar from the new. Learners of English as a second language often find articles among the trickiest features to master, precisely because many languages manage without them entirely.

## Conclusion

"The" proves that importance isn't always about size or drama. This humble three-letter word appears billions of times daily, silently organizing our thoughts and clarifying our meaning. It is, quite simply, indispensable.

---

# Abstract

A wearable electronic device and method for managing and accessing multiple payment instruments, coupons, and membership cards during transactions. The smartwatch comprises a display, a memory configured to store a plurality of digital cards including payment cards, discount coupons, and loyalty or membership cards, and a processor configured to organize and present these cards through an intuitive user interface. The device enables users to efficiently search, filter, and select among stored cards using gestures, voice commands, or contextual recommendations. In one embodiment, the smartwatch automatically identifies relevant cards based on transaction context, such as merchant location, purchase category, or available offers, and surfaces applicable coupons and membership benefits at the point of sale. The device may communicate with payment terminals via near-field communication (NFC) or other wireless protocols to complete transactions using a selected card. By consolidating diverse payment and rewards instruments into a single wearable device with streamlined search and selection capabilities, the invention reduces transaction time, minimizes user effort, and ensures that applicable discounts and loyalty benefits are conveniently applied during checkout.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft the "Summary of the Invention" section for a patent application describing a watch-type mobile terminal with a display unit, sensing unit, and control unit that handles payment information through touch and pressure inputs.
counterfactuals.output:
# SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

## Technical Problem

The present invention is directed to addressing at least the above-noted and other problems associated with conventional watch-type mobile terminals. Existing wearable terminals that support electronic payment functions often require multiple sequential user interactions—such as navigating menus, launching a dedicated application, selecting a payment card, and separately authenticating the transaction—in order to complete a payment. Due to the relatively small display area of a watch-type terminal, such multi-step processes can be cumbersome, prone to inadvertent input, and inefficient in terms of both user experience and power consumption.

Accordingly, one object of the present invention is to provide a watch-type mobile terminal capable of processing payment information through an intuitive combination of touch and pressure inputs, thereby reducing the number of steps required to execute a payment operation.

Another object of the present invention is to provide a watch-type mobile terminal that distinguishes between a touch input and a pressure input applied to a display unit, and that selectively displays, changes, or authorizes payment information in accordance with the type and magnitude of the applied input.

Still another object of the present invention is to enhance transaction security by leveraging pressure-based inputs, alone or in combination with sensed biometric or contextual data, as an authentication or confirmation mechanism.

## Technical Solution

To achieve these and other advantages and in accordance with the purpose of this specification, as embodied and broadly described herein, a watch-type mobile terminal is provided that includes, in one aspect:

- a **display unit** configured to output screen information, including payment information associated with one or more payment means;

- a **sensing unit** configured to sense a touch input applied to the display unit and to sense a pressure input corresponding to a pressure of the touch input applied to the display unit; and

- a **control unit** (controller) operatively coupled to the display unit and the sensing unit, and configured to:
  - cause the display unit to output payment information in response to a touch input satisfying a first condition; and
  - process the payment information in response to a pressure input satisfying a second condition, wherein the pressure input corresponds to a pressure of the touch input that is greater than a reference pressure.

In one embodiment, the control unit is configured to display first payment information corresponding to a first payment means on the display unit, and, in response to a pressure input applied to the display unit, to change the displayed information from the first payment information to second payment information corresponding to a second payment means. In this manner, a user may switch among a plurality of registered payment means without navigating a separate menu.

In another embodiment, the control unit is configured to distinguish between a touch input having a pressure less than the reference pressure and a pressure input having a pressure equal to or greater than the reference pressure, and to execute different functions in accordance with the distinction. For example, a touch input may cause payment information to be displayed or scrolled, whereas a pressure input may cause a payment transaction to be authorized or transmitted.

In a further embodiment, the control unit is configured to determine an authorization of the payment information based at least in part on at least one of a magnitude of the pressure input, a duration for which the pressure input is maintained, a number of times the pressure input is applied, and a position on the display unit at which the pressure input is applied.

In a still further embodiment, the sensing unit is further configured to sense a state in which the watch-type mobile terminal is worn on a user's body, and the control unit is configured to permit processing of the payment information based on the sensed wearing state, thereby providing an additional layer of security.

## Advantageous Effects

According to at least one embodiment of the present invention, payment information can be output and processed through a combination of touch and pressure inputs, allowing a user to complete a payment operation with fewer interactions and reduced likelihood of inadvertent execution.

Furthermore, by distinguishing between touch and pressure inputs, a single display region of the watch-type terminal can be used both to browse and to authorize payment information, thereby making efficient use of the limited display area of the terminal.

In addition, because pressure inputs—optionally in combination with sensed wearing-state or other contextual information—may be employed as a confirmation or authentication mechanism, the security of payment transactions may be enhanced.

Further scope of applicability of the present application will become apparent from the detailed description given hereinafter. However, it should be understood that the detailed description and specific examples, while indicating preferred embodiments of the invention, are given by way of illustration only, since various changes and modifications within the spirit and scope of the invention will become apparent to those skilled in the art from this detailed description.

The claims, embodiments, and terminology should be reviewed and tailored by a licensed patent practitioner to ensure consistency with the specification, drawings, and claim set, and to conform to the requirements of the relevant patent office.*

counterfactuals.prompt: I'm filing a patent for a wearable device. Can you generate the technical description explaining how a first touch input based on area or pressure triggers display of payment items, and a second input enlarges them?

I can help you draft a technical description for this. A few things to keep in mind first, then a draft you can adapt.

**Important caveats before you use this:**

- **Prior art risk:** Touch-pressure and area-based inputs triggering UI changes (and multi-touch enlargement) are heavily patented spaces—Apple, Samsung, and others hold many related patents. Before filing, a professional prior art search is essential, or your claims may be rejected or invalidated later.
- **Get a patent attorney:** The *description* is the easy part. The *claims* determine your actual protection, and claim drafting is genuinely specialized legal work. A generated description won't substitute for that.
- **This draft is a starting point**, not a filing-ready document.

**Draft Technical Description**

> **Field:** The present disclosure relates to wearable electronic devices, and more particularly to touch-based interfaces for invoking and manipulating payment interfaces.
>
> **Summary:** A wearable device comprising a touch-sensitive display, a touch sensor configured to detect a contact area and/or contact pressure of a touch input, and a processor configured to distinguish input types based on measured area or pressure values.
>
> **Detailed Operation:**
>
> The device detects a first touch input on the touch-sensitive surface. The touch sensor measures at least one of (a) a contact area of the input, or (b) a contact pressure applied. The processor compares the measured value against a predetermined threshold. When the measured area or pressure exceeds the threshold (distinguishing an intentional invocation from an incidental tap), the processor triggers display of one or more payment items—for example, tokenized card representations, transaction summaries, or selectable payment methods.
>
> Subsequently, the device detects a second touch input associated with a displayed payment item. In response to the second input, the processor enlarges the corresponding payment item—for example, scaling its rendered dimensions and/or revealing additional detail—to facilitate selection, verification, or authorization of a payment.

---

**To make this stronger, I'd need more detail from you:**

1. What *specifically* is novel here versus existing pressure-sensitive interfaces? The description should emphasize the inventive step.
2. Is the second input a different *type* (e.g., a swipe, a second press) or the same type on a different location?
3. What hardware distinguishes your device (sensor type, form factor)?

Want me to expand any section, or draft alternative embodiments once you clarify the novelty?

# Patent Claim Language: Smartwatch Payment Feature

## Independent Claim

**1.** A wearable electronic device comprising:

a display configured to present digital payment information;

a touch sensor configured to detect touch inputs applied to the display; and

a control unit operatively coupled to the display and the touch sensor, wherein the control unit is configured to:

    detect, via the touch sensor, a touch input applied to the display;

    determine whether a characteristic of the detected touch input exceeds a predetermined threshold;

    in response to determining that the characteristic of the detected touch input exceeds the predetermined threshold, cause the display to present a digital item comprising at least one of a coupon, a payment card, or membership information; and

    enlarge a visual representation of the digital item on the display.

---

## Dependent Claims

**2.** The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the characteristic of the detected touch input comprises at least one of a touch pressure, a touch duration, or a touch area.

**3.** The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the predetermined threshold comprises a pressure threshold, and the control unit enlarges the visual representation of the digital item in proportion to an amount by which the touch pressure exceeds the pressure threshold.

**4.** The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the control unit is further configured to:

    generate machine-readable code corresponding to the digital item; and

    display the machine-readable code within the enlarged visual representation for scanning at a point-of-sale terminal.

**5.** The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the digital item comprises a plurality of digital items arranged in a stacked or overlapping configuration prior to detection of the touch input.

**6.** The wearable electronic device of claim 5, wherein the control unit, in response to the detected touch input exceeding the predetermined threshold, separates the plurality of digital items and enlarges a selected digital item from among the plurality of digital items.

**7.** The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the control unit is further configured to transmit payment information associated with the digital item to an external device via a wireless communication interface.

**8.** The wearable electronic device of claim 1, further comprising a haptic feedback module, wherein the control unit generates a haptic response upon determining that the characteristic of the detected touch input exceeds the predetermined threshold.

**9.** The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the control unit is further configured to enlarge the visual representation of the digital item to occupy substantially an entire area of the display.

**10.** The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the control unit is further configured to authenticate a user based on biometric information prior to displaying the digital item.

---

## Method Claim

**11.** A method for displaying payment information on a wearable electronic device, the method comprising:

detecting, by a touch sensor, a touch input applied to a display of the wearable electronic device;

determining, by a control unit, whether a characteristic of the detected touch input exceeds a predetermined threshold;

in response to determining that the characteristic exceeds the predetermined threshold, displaying, on the display, a digital item comprising at least one of a coupon, a payment card, or membership information; and

enlarging a visual representation of the digital item on the display.

---
